previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of renal transplant failure was admitted for fever and rigors following manipulation of his tunneled dialysis line. He was found to have MSSA bacteremia, and the infected line was exchanged over a guidewire. Blood and catheter tip cultures confirmed Staphylococcus aureus, and he was transitioned from vancomycin and gentamicin to cefazolin, which he will continue for four weeks. Repeat blood cultures remained negative, and a transthoracic echocardiogram showed no evidence of endocarditis. Tacrolimus was discontinued as it was no longer needed post-transplant failure. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home in stable condition with plans for ongoing antibiotic administration during dialysis and close monitoring for recurrence.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with fever and chills.

___.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral radiographs of the chest demonstrate clear lungs
without consolidation or edema.  There are no pleural effusions or
pneumothorax.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

LIMITED LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND

COMPARISON:  ___.

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease, on hemodialysis with fistula in left upper
extremity.  Evaluate for abnormal fluid collection or abscess at graft site.

FINDINGS:  Limited, focused ultrasound of the left upper extremity was
performed in the area of dialysis graft.  There is normal color flow within
the graft.  There is no evidence of abnormal fluid collection or edema
surrounding the graft site.  The brachial vessels were partially imaged and
demonstrated normal compression.

IMPRESSION:  No focal fluid collection seen.

INDICATIONS:  ___ male with bilateral hallux ulcerations.  Please
perform peripheral vascular studies.

Bilateral lower extremity ABIs, Doppler waveforms, and PVRs were performed at
rest.

FINDINGS:

RIGHT:  The right ABI is 1.0 at both ___ and DP.  The right-sided Doppler
waveforms are triphasic to the level of the popliteal with monophasic
waveforms at the posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis levels.  Right-sided PVRs
show significant artifact at the ankle level, but there is a significant
decline between calf and metatarsal where the amplitude is blunted.

The left ABI is 1.0/0.9 at the ___ and DP, respectively.  Left-sided Doppler
waveforms are triphasic to the popliteal level and are monophasic at the
posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis.  Left-sided PVRs are symmetric when
compared to the right and show a decline between calf and metatarsal level
suggestive of tibial occlusive disease.

IMPRESSION:  Suspect slightly, falsely elevated ABIs.  Doppler waveforms and
PVRs would suggest mild-to-moderate tibial occlusive disease at rest.
